title: Lift, Splat, Shoot: Encoding Images From Arbitrary Camera Rigs by Implicitly Unprojecting to 3D
layout_note: Geometric explainer: perspective camera-ray sketch on the left turned into a heat-map matrix on the right.
grouping: Two parts without containers: a ray diagram on the left and a matrix on the right, joined by two black arrows (one from the depth bars, one from the feature column).
shapes_depth: A street photo is drawn in perspective as a tilted plane; thin light-blue rays fan from a black camera icon at the bottom right to the image. Along one ray, depth bins are drawn as slanted dark-blue bars of different lengths with black dots at the bin centres (labelled 'depth distribution alpha'); a short vertical bar of four blue shades is the feature 'c'. The lifted feature is a wide matrix of cells shaded light-to-dark blue, column headers alpha_0 c, alpha_1 c ... alpha_D c, with black dimension brackets 'D' (bottom) and 'C' (right) and the caption 'per-pixel outer product'.
proposed_highlight: Single-concept figure: the depth distribution is the emphasised object, drawn as the longest dark bars and echoed by the darkest column of the matrix.
lesson: Draw per-pixel depth as bars of different length laid along the camera ray, then show the lifted feature as a blue-shaded depth x channel matrix with dimension brackets, so the depth peak reappears as the matrix's darkest column.
notes: Venue ECCV 2020 from the arXiv comment (venue_source: arxiv-journal-ref). The whole figure is a single raster image in the PDF (refs crop recorded one embedded image covering the crop), so kb measure cannot separate photos from drawing: photo_share is null and the palette includes the embedded photos and renders.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: lifting image features to a 3-D frustum

core.what: the lift drawn on the camera geometry: rays fan from a camera icon to a street photo, and along one ray black depth points carry blue bars whose length is the depth distribution alpha

relations.form: light-blue rays from a camera icon at bottom right to the corners and pixels of a perspective street image at left; one ray marked with discrete black depth points, each with a slanted blue bar

two diagonal arrows carry the depth distribution alpha and the 4-cell feature vector c into a D x C grid at right, its columns labelled alpha_0 c, alpha_1 c, ..., alpha_D c and captioned 'per-pixel outer product'

channels.colour: blue intensity = magnitude: bar length/shade for depth probability, cell shade for feature value and for the product in the grid; light-blue thin lines = camera rays
channels.shape: black dots = depth bins on a ray; slanted bars = per-bin probability; cell grid = the lifted frustum feature for one pixel
channels.line: thin light-blue = camera rays; black arrows = values combined into the outer product
channels.frame: brackets with D and C mark the grid's axes

quality.strengths: The operation is drawn on its structure: discrete depths along a real camera ray, and the outer product as an actual D x C grid whose darkest column matches the most probable depth, so the reader sees the feature being placed at a depth.
quality.weaknesses: The label 'depth distribution alpha' sits beside the ray while a separate 4-cell column is labelled 'feature c', and the two arrows into the grid start from loosely placed points, so which arrow carries alpha and which c is not explicit; only one ray of the image is lifted.

insights.structure: Two halves: on the left a tilted street photo with rays fanning from a camera icon and bars along one ray; on the right a C x D heat-map grid labeled 'per-pixel outer product'.
insights.data: Depth distribution alpha is drawn as blue bars of varying length along the ray and as a vertical colour strip, feature c as a second strip; their product is a blue-shaded matrix with columns alpha_0 c ... alpha_D c.
insights.emphasis: The darkest column in the matrix matches the longest bar on the ray, visually tying the peak depth to where the feature is placed.
insights.flow: Two black arrows lead from the alpha and c strips into the matrix, left to right; rays converge on the camera at bottom right.

arrangement.units: one unboxed scene: a perspective camera sketch beside a labeled matrix with dimension brackets
arrangement.inputs_as: real street photo on a tilted image plane
